title: Vitamin C is one of the lipolytic substances in green tea.
text_summary: 我们研究了绿茶中的维生素C对分化良好的3T3-L1细胞脂肪分解的影响。当成熟脂肪细胞接触维生素 C 时，甘油三酯浓度降低 (p < 0.05)，并且甘油磷酸脱氢酶（脂肪转化标志物）的活性显着受到抑制 (p < 0.01)。这些数据表明，绿茶可能具有脂肪分解活性，因为绿茶中所含的维生素 C 具有抑制甘油三酯积累的机制。

PHYTOTHERAPY RESEARCH
          Phytother. Res. 16, S91–S92 (2002)
          Published online in Wiley InterScience (www.interscience.wiley.com). DOI: 10.1002/ptr.843


    Vitamin C is one of the Lipolytic Substances in
   Green Tea


      Noboru Hasegawa,* Nami Niimi and Fumiko Odani

          Department of Food and Nutrition Nagoya Bunri College, Nagoya, Japan


     We have studied the inﬂuence of vitamin C contained in green tea on the lipolysis of well-differentiated
       3T3-L1 cells. When mature adipocytes were exposed to vitamin C the triglyceride concentration was
        decreased (p   0.05) and the activity of glycerophosphate dehydrogenase, a marker of adipose conver-
          sion, was signiﬁcantly inhibited (p   0.01). These data suggest that green tea may have a lipolytic activity
       due to the mechanism by which the vitamin C contained in it inhibits triglyceride accumulation. Copy-

MATERIALS AND METHODS

Chemicals. Vitamin C was purchased from Wako Pure
Chemical  (Osaka,  Japan) and  used  as  an  aqueous
solution. Dulbecco’s modiﬁed Eagle’s medium (DMEM)
and DMEM: Ham F-12  (1:1) were purchased from
Dainihon Pharmaceutical Co. (Tokyo, Japan). Bovine
insulin, calf serum (CS) and fetal calf serum (FCS) were
from JRH Biosciences (Lunexa, KS).

Cell culture. 3T3-L1 preadipocytes were cultured by the
method  previously  described (Hasegawa  and  Mori,
2000). Brieﬂy, cells were grown in DMEM containing
10% CS, 100 U/mL penicillin and 10  g/mL strepto-
mycin, at 37°C in a humidiﬁed 5% CO2. At conﬂuence
(day 0), the medium was changed to DMEM:F-12 (1:1)
containing 10% FCS, and differentiation was induced

                                       RESULTS AND DISCUSSION

                                                                                  It was reported earlier that when mature adipocytes were
                                                      exposed to 0.1 mg/mL of powdered green tea, smaller
                                                            intracytoplasmic lipid droplets selectively disappeared
                                                   (Hasegawa and Mori, 2000). In the present study, when
                                                            0.3 g/mL of vitamin C was added at the same concen-
                                                                   tration as powdered green tea, there was a signiﬁcant
                                                          decrease in the triglyceride content (Fig. 1) and GPDH
                                                                   activity  (Fig.  2). When a lower dose of vitamin C
                                                            (0.18  g/mL) was added, GPDH activity was decreased
                                                               signiﬁcantly, and the triglyceride content tended to be
                                                            decreased. These results suggest that the lipolytic effect
                                                            of vitamin C  is via the mechanism that inhibits  tri-
                                                             glyceride accumulation.
                                                        There is some evidence that catechin or caffeine can
                                                       inﬂuence the adipocyte triglyceride level. Catechin was
                                                      found to inhibit triglyceride accumulation in 3T3-L1 cells
                                                  by inhibiting acetyl-CoA carboxylase activity (Watanabe
